meta.title: Airline operations at the airport
meta.description: How Kestrel Air gets passengers and their bags from the terminal door onto a flight at Northgate Airport; open check-in, baggage or boarding for the detail.

summary.headline: Passengers and bags travel separately and meet again only on the aircraft; the departure control system keeps the two in step.
points: Every check-in, bag and boarding scan is recorded in the departure control system
A bag only flies if its passenger has boarded
Check-in, Baggage and Boarding each open a detail diagram; Baggage goes one level deeper into the sorter

data.title: Check-in
data.subtitle: App, kiosk or desk
data.description: Confirms the passenger, collects passport data and issues the boarding pass. Open it for the three ways in.

data.title: Security
data.subtitle: Run by the airport
data.description: Airport staff screen passengers and cabin bags. The airline only sees the boarding pass scan.

data.title: Boarding
data.subtitle: Gate to aircraft door
data.description: Scans boarding passes, closes the flight and sends the final figures to load control. Open it for the gate in detail.

data.title: Baggage
data.subtitle: Screen, sort, load
data.description: Takes hold bags from bag drop to the aircraft hold. Open it for the baggage hall, then the sorter inside it.

data.title: Departure control
data.subtitle: Passengers, bags, seats
data.description: The airline's record of who checked in, which bags they dropped and who boarded.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Seven parts. Check-in, Baggage and Boarding carry a magnifier: each opens its own detail diagram.

steps.title: Check in
steps.description: The passenger checks in with their booking reference; the departure control system marks them as checked in.

steps.title: Passenger and bag part
steps.description: The passenger goes through security with a boarding pass; the tagged bag goes down to the baggage hall.

steps.title: The bag is loaded
steps.description: Baggage loads the bag into the hold and reports it to departure control. Open Baggage to follow it through the sorter.

steps.title: Board and close
steps.description: The gate checks each boarding pass against the passenger list. Only when the counts match does the flight close.

meta.title: Check-in
meta.description: Three ways to check in, one record in departure control, and passport data sent to the border agency.

data.title: Check-in desk
data.subtitle: Agent, for special cases
data.description: Unaccompanied minors, wheelchairs, pets and passengers whose documents need a check by eye.

data.title: Border agency
data.subtitle: Advance passenger data
data.description: Receives each passenger's passport details and can refuse boarding before the passenger reaches the gate.

data.title: Bag drop
data.subtitle: Weigh, tag, belt
data.description: Weighs each bag against the allowance, prints the tag and sends the bag down the belt to the baggage hall.

steps.title: Inside check-in
steps.description: Three channels feed one record in departure control, which talks to the border agency and the bag drop.

steps.title: Pick a channel
steps.description: Most passengers use the app; the desk is kept for cases that need a person.

steps.title: Send passport data
steps.description: Passport details go to the border agency; a refusal stops the boarding pass from being issued.

steps.title: Drop the bag
steps.description: Bag drop checks the weight against the allowance in departure control, then tags the bag.

meta.title: Baggage hall
meta.description: How a hold bag is screened, sorted and loaded; open the sorter for the next level down.

data.title: CT scanner
data.subtitle: Every hold bag
data.description: Clears about 97% of bags automatically; the rest go to a screener.

data.title: Sorter
data.subtitle: Routes bag to its flight
data.description: Reads the bag tag and sends the bag to the chute for its flight. Open it for the sorter in detail.

data.title: Bag reconciliation
data.subtitle: Is the owner on board?
data.description: Matches every loaded bag to a boarded passenger. A bag whose owner does not board is taken off.

steps.title: Inside the baggage hall
steps.description: Screening and sorting sit in the hall; loading happens on the apron. The sorter opens a further level.

steps.title: Screen the bag
steps.description: Every bag goes through the CT scanner; bags it cannot clear are reviewed by a screener.

steps.title: Sort to the flight
steps.description: Cleared bags reach the sorter, which drops each one at its flight's make-up area. Open the sorter for how it decides.

steps.title: Load and reconcile
steps.description: Containers are driven to the aircraft; each bag is scanned into the hold and matched to a boarded passenger.

meta.title: Baggage sorter
meta.description: How the sorter reads a bag tag and decides where the bag goes.

data.title: Manual coding
data.subtitle: Agent keys the tag
data.description: Bags whose tag cannot be read are diverted here; an agent types the ten-digit tag number.

data.title: Sort control
data.subtitle: Tag to destination
data.description: Looks up the tag in the bag messages from departure control and picks a destination.

steps.title: Inside the sorter
steps.description: A reader, a control system and a loop of tilting trays decide where each bag goes.

steps.title: Read the tag
steps.description: The arch reads the tag; the rare bag it cannot read is coded by hand.

steps.title: Choose a destination
steps.description: Sort control matches the tag to its flight and tells the tray where to tip.

steps.title: Tip the tray
steps.description: A bag for a flight that is not yet open waits in the early bag store; otherwise it drops into the flight chute.

meta.title: Boarding
meta.description: How the gate boards a flight, closes it and hands the final figures to load control.

data.title: Gate agent
data.subtitle: Calls no-shows, closes flight
data.description: Calls passengers who have checked in but not boarded, and closes the flight 15 minutes before departure.

data.title: Offload bags
data.subtitle: No-show passengers
data.description: The ramp team takes off the bags of anyone who did not board, before the doors close.

data.title: Load control
data.subtitle: Weight and balance
data.description: Turns the final passenger and bag figures into the loadsheet the captain signs.

steps.title: Inside boarding
steps.description: From the first scan at the gate to the loadsheet in the cockpit.

steps.title: Scan the passes
steps.description: Each scan marks the passenger as boarded; departure control lists those still missing.

steps.title: Deal with no-shows
steps.description: A passenger who does not come has their bags taken off; a bag never flies without its owner.

steps.title: Close the flight
steps.description: Once the counts match, the agent closes the flight and load control sends the loadsheet to the crew.
